title: Symmetry-Aware Bayesian Optimization via Max Kernels
claim: Our invariant kernel captures the true symmetry structure of the function, while the common averaged kernel only approximates it.
layout: 3 heatmap panels, left-to-right, shared colormap style, function then two kernels
description: Three side-by-side heatmap panels with titles above. The left panel, 'Radial-Invariant Function', shows concentric rings in a purple-to-yellow colormap, with a dark spot at the center, to illustrate a function that depends only on radius. The center panel shows k_max(x, x') as a function of ||x||₂ (horizontal axis) and ||x'||₂ (vertical axis). It has a bright yellow diagonal band, so similarity is high wherever the two norms are equal, and it fades to blue and purple away from the diagonal. The right panel shows k_avg(x, x') on the same axes. It has a smeared, asymmetric pattern, yellow only in the bottom-left corner, with no clean diagonal. The eye goes first to the rings, then to the crisp diagonal in the center panel, which contrasts with the blurry right panel.
caption: (Left) A two-dimensional function f⋆(x) invariant under planar rotations (see (16)): if ∥x∥2 = ∥x′∥2, then f⋆(x) = f⋆(x′). (Center/Right) Rotation-invariant kernels derived from an RBF base kernel (lengthscale 1/2), visualized as a function of (∥x∥2, ∥x′∥2). kmax (center) captures the correct invariance, while kavg (right) only approximates it.
abstract: Bayesian Optimization (BO) is a powerful framework for optimizing noisy, expensive-to-evaluate black-box functions. When the objective exhibits invariances under a group action, exploiting these symmetries can substantially improve BO efficiency. While using maximum similarity across group orbits has long been considered in other domains, the fact that the max kernel is not positive semidefinite (PSD) has prevented its use in BO. In this work, we revisit this idea by considering a PSD projection of the max kernel. Compared to existing invariant (and non-invariant) kernels, we show it achieves significantly lower regret on both synthetic and real-world BO benchmarks, without increasing computational complexity.
